changelog: - **Write-path capability gate on the placements module, and a check that keeps it complete** (#2364, epic #2348). #2351 dropped `/admin/offers`, `/admin/requisitions`, `/admin/interview-requests` and `/interviews` from the sidebar of a vertical without `placements`, and #2352 gated the mentorship modules — but the placement routes themselves were still reachable by a direct POST. All ten mutating handlers (`/api/offers` POST + `[id]` PATCH, `/api/requisitions` POST + `[id]` PATCH, `/api/interview-requests` POST + `[id]` PATCH, `/api/interview-panels` POST + `[id]` PATCH + `[id]/close` + `[id]/reopen`) now call `requireCapability(session.user.orgId, 'placements')` immediately after their session check and before any role check, validation or write, so a refused tenant gets `403 { code: 'capability_unavailable', capability }` rather than a 400 that leaks the shape of a module it does not have. Panel SCORING stays under `evaluations` (#2352) because it writes `Evaluation` rows; convening a panel is the placement. Two writers are deliberately left open and documented: `expireOffers()` (the cron expiry sweep — sessionless by design, and an already-sent offer should still stop being open) and the `InterviewRequest` re-pointing inside the duplicate-user merge (an identity operation that creates no placement). The leaked-writer class had been caught twice by human review and never by a check, so `npm run check:capability-writers` now walks back from every write to a gated model to the handler that reaches it and fails CI when there is no gate in between — including a second handler added to an already-gated file; the guard has its own unit tests for both the too-narrow and the too-broad direction. INTERNSHIP carries `placements`, so this is a strict no-op for today's product, asserted by the INTERNSHIP half of `e2e/vertical-write-gate.spec.ts`.
